newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market held steady in quiet trade on Thursday, dealers said.

They said although the market closed with a Z$77 million surplus on Wednesday, not many maturities were expected on Thursday to add to liquidity and thus the central Reserve Bank had as a result not auctioned any treasury bills.

Meanwhile, discount houses were selling the central bank paper in the secondary market unchanged at 16.25 percent and NCDs redeemable after after 30, 60 and 90 days were also quoted steady at 17.25 and 17 percent (buying and selling respectively).
Bankers acceptance rates were at 16.60 percent (buying) and were selling at 16.35 percent, while call money was indicated at around 16 percent.
